ROLL CALL: At 6:10 p.m., on Monday, June 22, 2026, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, City Attorney Montes,
City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of
Community Development Ho, Planning Manager McCurley, Economic Development Specialist
MacCarley, Director of Public Works and Utilities Ahlen, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Chief
of Police Kennedy, Director of Library Services LohGuan, Director of Human Resources Ko,
Management Analyst – Sustainability Martel, Management Analyst Alvarez

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maloney

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to
prioritize respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples
throughout California, especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with
respect and gratitude for the Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the
caretakers of this land. It is through their examples that we are reminded of our greater
responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take care of each other.

CEREMONIALS

1.  COMMENDATIONS: ENVIRONMENTAL SCHOLARSHIP AWARD RECIPIENTS –
  F2M26-3
  Mayor Maloney and City Council wished to commend the recent winners of the Fifth
  Annual Environmental Scholarship Award. Republic Services joined with the City of
  Alhambra to award five scholarships of $1,000 to Alhambra students. Each finalist
  submitted an essay based on the theme of environmental stewardship and acknowledged
  the power of future generations to innovate greener living standards, an environmentally
  sound economy, and an environmentally sustainable lifestyle. The City of Alhambra was
  pleased to congratulate Alhambra students Siqi Li, Keiko Rakin, Joyce Li, Gideon
  Schneider and Emilie Taniguchi for their achievements and for inspiring others through
  their dedication to the conservation of our planet. Mayor Maloney presented
  commendations to the scholarship award recipients.

2.  CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE: MABLE YU – F2M26-3
  Mayor Maloney and the City Council wished to commend and thank Revenue Supervisor
  Mable Yu who recently retired after 38 years of faithful and loyal service to the Finance
  Department and the City of Alhambra. Mayor Maloney presented a Certificate of Service

6-22-26
   plaque to Ms. Yu for her outstanding work for the City. Ms. YU thanked Council for the
  recognition and spoke about her long career with the City of Alhambra.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

3.  ADOPTION OF THE 2025 URBAN WATER MANAGEMENT PLAN – F2M11-37, N2M26-
  56, M2M26-107

  Director of Public Works and Utilities AHLEN delivered a staff report. This was the time
  and place set by Notice No. N2M26-56 for the City Council to hold a public hearing on the
  proposed 2025 Urban Water Management Plan. Stan CHEN, from Stetson Engineers,
  provided a presentation. The California Department of Water Resources requires every
  urban water supplier to prepare and adopt an Urban Water Management Plan (UWMP),
  including a Water Shortage Contingency Plan, and periodically update the Urban Water
  Management Plan at least once every five years, in years ending in six and one. The 2025
  Urban Water Management Plan and Water Shortage Contingency Plan were prepared
  pursuant to the “Urban Water Management Planning Act” and the California Water Code
  and requires adoption by July 2026. The 2025 UWMP is an update to the City’s most
  recent plan dated June 2020, which was prepared in accordance with the UWMP Act,
  2
6-22-26
   California Water Code. Staff reviewed the 2020 Plan and with the assistance of Stetson
  Engineering Inc., provided updated information such as population, number of metered
  services, water pumped and distributed, annual future water demands, and the addition
  of required conservation information. The 2025 Urban Water Management Plan and
  related appendices can be viewed at:

  https://www.alhambraca.gov/DocumentCenter/View/7938/City-of-Alhambra---2025-UWMP-FINAL-DRAFT

  https://www.alhambraca.gov/DocumentCenter/View/7939/City-of-Alhambra---2025-UWMP-FINAL-DRAFT-
  APPENDICES

  Opened & Closed the Public Hearing: Mayor MALONEY opened the public hearing and as
  there was no one present who wished to speak, closed the same.

  Discussion:  Councilmember LEE discussed water contamination with Mr.
  CHEN. Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. AHLEN discussed the EPA installed
  groundwater wells and their regular monitoring system. Mr. AHLEN provided further
  clarification regarding testing of groundwater. Councilmember MAZA discussed reduced
  water usage and Mr. CHEN provided clarification. Councilmember WANG and Mr. AHLEN
  discussed imported water from other districts. Mayor MALONEY discussed his position as
  an alternate Board Member for the San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority. He
  discussed the water supply for Alhambra and ongoing projects to capture stormwater to
  replenish groundwater.

  Action Taken:  City Council conducted a public hearing and, after receiving public
  comment, adopted the 2025 Urban Water Management Plan; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M26-107)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  MAZA, LEE, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

4.  FISCAL YEAR 2026-27 APPROPRIATION LIMIT – F2M26-17, N2M26-65, R2M26-16,
  M2M26-82

  This was the time and place set by Notice No. N2M26-65 for the City Council to hold a
  public hearing on the Fiscal Year 2026-27 Appropriation Limit. Director of Finance LIEU
  delivered a staff report. Proposition XIII B (Gann Initiative) prohibits local agencies from
  exceeding their 1978-79 fiscal year appropriations after allowing for cost-of-living (CPI)
  and population changes which are certified by the State Department of Finance.
  Proposition 111 would allow the City to adjust its annual limits for the following factors,
  subject to approval by the City Council:
  a)  Either the California Per Capita Income or the percentage change in local
  assessment roll from the preceding year due to the addition of local nonresidential
  construction in the City.
  b)  Either the City’s own population growth or the population growth of the entire
  county.
  Government Code Section 7910 requires agencies to adopt a resolution each year
  disclosing their appropriation limit. In accordance with Proposition 111, the City is required
  to conduct a review of their appropriations limit during the annual financial audit. For Fiscal
  3
6-22-26
   Year 2024-2025, the City’s appropriation limit was reviewed by our auditors, Moss, Levy
  & Hartzheim, LLP, and determined to be properly calculated. The calculations in
  computing the City of Alhambra’s appropriation limit for the 2026-2027 fiscal year are on
  file in the Finance Department. The appropriation limit for the 2026-27 fiscal year was
  $211,535,544 and the applicable appropriation subject to this limitation is $91,357,095.
  Therefore, the City was favorably under the appropriations limit by $120,178,449.

  Opened & Closed the Public Hearing: Mayor MALONEY opened the public hearing and as
  there was no one present who wished to speak, closed the same.

  Discussion:  Mayor MALONEY spoke in support of the Item.

  Action Taken:  After receiving public testimony, the Mayor closed the public
  hearing and the City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M26-16 entitled: A Resolution of
  the Alhambra City Council establishing the Appropriation Limit for FY 2026-27 and
  approving the annual adjustment factors used in the calculation thereof; and, approve the
  annual adjustment factors (per capita income change +4.95% and City population change
  -0.20%) used in the calculation of the appropriation limit. (M2M26-82)

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded: WANG
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, WANG, MAZA, LEE, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  ANNUAL RECRUITMENT AND VACANCY REPORT – F2M26-2

  Director of Human Resources KO delivered a staff report. Governor Newsom signed AB
  2561 into law on September 22, 2024 to amend the Meyers-Milias Brown Act (MMBA).
  Effective January 1, 2025, AB 2561 added California Government Code Section 3502.3
  which would require public agencies to hold a public hearing at least once per fiscal year
  to report on vacancy and recruitment status and retention efforts. The public hearing
  presentation must be made prior to the adoption of the final budget for the fiscal year. The
  City’s previous report was presented at the City Council meeting of May 12, 2025. The
  City had 412 full-time positions budgeted with 19 of these positions vacant as of May 14,
  2026, for an approximately 4.6% overall vacancy rate. Within the past 12 months, City
  Human Resources staff worked closely with public safety police and fire to support and
  enhance recruitment strategies focused on hiring at the level of Police Recruit and Fire
  Paramedic Intern. Doing so would allow interested qualified candidates an opportunity to
  work in a job and internship work structure. These efforts support the City Council’s
  strategic goal to not only enhance public safety but also enhance transparency and open
  governance. City staff would continue efforts towards filling the remaining budgeted
  vacancies.

  Opened & Closed the Public Hearing: Mayor MALONEY opened the public hearing and as
  there was no one present who wished to speak, closed the same.

  Discussion:  Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. KO discussed the
  Alhambra City Employees Association. Councilmember WANG spoke in support of the
  report. Councilmember LEE discussed the existing bargaining units and the need to
  continue recruitment.

  4
6-22-26
   Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the annual report on recruitment and
  vacancy rates.

PRESENTATIONS

6.  HOUSING ELEMENT IMPLEMENTATION PROGRAM 11 (WORKFORCE HOUSING
  PROGRAM): REPORT AND PRESENTATION ON WORKFORCE HOUSING
  PROGRAM PLAN – F2M20-37, M2M26-101

  Director of Community Development HO delivered a staff report and Dima GALKIN of
  Harris Associates delivered a presentation. Housing Element Program 11 directs the City
  to develop a proposal for a Workforce Housing Program that may include employer-
  assisted housing opportunities, identification of financial resources specific to workforce
  housing, and other incentives and actions to preserve and produce workforce housing.
  The City partnered with the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments (SGVCOG)
  through its Affordable Housing Incubator Program, funded by the Southern California
  Association of Governments (SCAG) Regional Early Action Planning (REAP) 2.0
  Program, to develop the proposal for a Workforce Housing Program in Alhambra. Staff
  presented information about the Workforce Housing Program Plan which was prepared to
  help the City better understand local workforce housing needs and identify potential
  program components, partnerships, funding strategies, and implementation actions that
  the City may consider if it elects to establish a Workforce Housing Program Plan in the
  future.

  Public Comment:
  1) Shirley Tatsuno discussed the lack of affordable housing and the need for a Workforce
  Housing Program.

  2) Lewis McCammon, also provided a handout to Council, and discussed the lack of
  affordable housing and the need for a Workforce Housing Program.

  3) Melissa Michelson supported affordable housing but expressed concerns with the in-
  fill sites and the impact on historic preservation of older properties. She suggested
  adaptively reuse available housing stock and provide incentives for existing property
  owners to enroll in the program.

  4) Alborz Mohtashami, via Zoom, spoke in support of the Workforce Housing Program
  and suggesting increasing the AMI. He discussed naturally occurring workforce
  housing through upzoning and increasing density.

  Discussion:  Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER spoke in support of the Program.
  She discussed the “missing middle” development projects, the San Gabriel Valley Housing
  Trust, and eligibility standards as laid out in the Program. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and
  Mr. GALKIN discussed the available developers for supportive housing projects. Mr.
  GALKIN provided clarification regarding funding sources. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER
  motioned to approve the Workforce Housing Program Plan.

  Councilmember WANG discussed affordability issues and supported the Plan. She also
  discussed the “missing middle” support for moderate income families.

  5
6-22-26
   Councilmember MAZA spoke in support of the Plan and discussed Affordable Housing
  and housing affordability.

  Councilmember LEE also discussed the “missing middle” and non-profit developers of
  projects. Mr. GALKIN provided clarification. She also discussed in-fill sites with Mr.
  GALKIN. Mr. HO provided clarification regarding the selection of in-fill sites. Ms. LEE and
  Mr. GALKIN also discussed historic preservation and preserving affordability of housing.

  Action Taken:  City Council received a presentation on the Workforce Housing
  Program Plan, approve eligibility ranges in the Executive Summary of the Workforce
  Housing Program Plan as outlined in the June 22, 2026 staff report by the Director of
  Community Development and directed staff as deemed appropriate. (M2M26-101)

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded: MAZA
  Ayes:  WANG, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  REVIEW OF THE MIDWICK PARK / ALHAMBRA HILLS TRACT PREFERRED
  PARKING DISTRICT – F2M26-7, F2M15-59

  Management Analyst ALVAREZ delivered a staff report. On December 14, 2015, the City
  Council adopted Resolution No. R2M15-29 establishing the Midwick Park / Alhambra Hills
  Tract Preferred Parking District (PPD) in response to neighborhood parking concerns
  associated with spillover student parking from California State University, Los Angeles
  (CSULA). The PPD was established following resident petitions, community outreach, and
  neighborhood surveys indicating support for parking restrictions within the affected
  residential area. On May 11, 2026, Vice Mayor Andrade-Stadler requested that staff
  agendize a review of the existing PPD restrictions and evaluate the potential expansion of
  the District to address ongoing parking concerns raised by residents related to the nearby
  Los Angeles Football Club (LAFC) training facility. LAFC opened after the PPD was
  created. Since the May 11th meeting, staff received numerous calls from residents in the
  PPD, particularly those that were interested in having their street removed from the PPD
  because there is no longer an issue. As such, staff recommended community outreach be
  conducted for all properties in the current PPD, to determine if the boundaries should be
  reduced, and if the days/hours of the remaining PPD should be expanded to include
  Saturday and Sunday to regulate LAFC parking.

  Public Comment:
  1) Gabriel Gutierrez spoke regarding the Alhambra Hills Tract and the history of parking
  issues. He suggested more consistent parking enforcement.

  2) Manny Armas requested more consistent parking enforcement.

  3) Henry Aviles, via Zoom, requested that Charnwood Ave. south of Julep Place, be
  removed from the preferred parking district.

  4) Randye Kay, via Zoom, requested a preferred parking district for her neighborhood at
  Midwickhill.

  5) Rita Ledesma, via Zoom, sent a petition from neighbors to remove Winthrop Drive
  6
6-22-26
   (Warwick Road to Westboro Avenue) from the CSULA Parking District.

  Discussion:  Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER supported staff undertaking
  community outreach and surveys in the Midwick Park/Alhambra Hills Tract Preferred
  Parking District. She recommended surveys take place during the LAFC scheduled
  season and during soccer activities.

  Councilmember MAZA discussed the history of the Preferred Parking District. He
  suggested staff continue to communicate with LAFC and CalState LA regarding parking
  restrictions. Mr. MAZA and City Manager BINNQUIST discussed the preferred parking
  district fees and restrictions. Ms. BINNQUIST discussed some of the conflicting feedback
  received from residents and provided clarification regarding parking enforcement in the
  district. Mr. MAZA supported the survey of residents.

  Councilmember WANG and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed the permitting process and
  restrictions. Ms. BINNQUIST clarified the information staff could gather and present to
  Council.

  Councilmember LEE discussed the permitting process and suggested guest passes could
  be issues like overnight parking permit. Ms. BINNQUIST provided clarification regarding
  a new virtual permit system.

  Council confirmed with Ms. Binnquist that they would like staff to undertake community
  outreach in the preferred parking district to determine participation, boundaries, potential
  expansion, and process. Staff would return with the results of the survey and make
  recommendations. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER reiterated the need to conduct the surveys
  between June and September. Ms. BINNQUIST provided further clarification.

  Action Taken:  City Council directed staff to undertake community outreach in the
  Midwick Park / Alhambra Hills Tract Preferred Parking District to determine the necessary
  boundaries and potential expansion of days for the District. No vote was required.

8.  POTENTIAL PREFERRED PARKING DISTRICT ADJACENT TO THE COURTYARD
  BY MARRIOTT – F2M26-7

  Management Analyst ALVAREZ delivered a staff report. On May 11, 2026, during public
  comment, numerous residents expressed concern about spillover parking associated with
  the nearby Courtyard by Marriott. During Council Communications, Councilmember Wang
  requested an item to discuss parking concerns and a Preferred Parking District (PPD) at
  the next City Council meeting. Alhambra Municipal Code Chapter 11.29 allows for the City
  Council to establish Preferred Parking Districts. The City currently has a PPD in the
  Midwick Park I Alhambra Hills neighborhood adjacent to CSULA, and another in the
  Hellman and 9th neighborhood adjacent to the Atlantic Time Square project. Outreach,
  including a survey, could be utilized to get resident preferences regarding boundaries and
  the days/times parking would be restricted if a PPD were to be established.

  Public Comment:
  1) Martha Yoselentz spoke in favor of a preferred parking district. She noted she
  preferred hang tags.

  7
6-22-26
   2) Caleb Kwok spoke against a preferred parking district without further study and
  outreach to neighboring Monterey Park residents.

  3) Carolyn Johansen spoke in favor of a preferred parking district.

  4) Weixiang Zhu, via Mandarin translator from the Language Line interpretation service,
  requested clarification regarding speed limits in the neighborhood. Mr. ZHU also
  discussed the parking issues in the area and requested more consistent enforcement.
  Mr. ZHU also discussed pedestrian issues and tree trimming issues.

  Discussion:  Councilmember WANG discussed the background of the issue and
  feedback she received with residents regarding safety and neighborhood access issues
  due to overcrowded parking. Ms. WANG suggested staff review the creation of a preferred
  parking district in the area and assess the safety concerns raised by residents including
  driveway access, line of sight, driveway visibility, corner visibility, speeding concerns, and
  potential pedestrian safety improvements. She also suggested enforcement of parking
  restrictions. She suggested staff reach out Monterey Park residents and the City of
  Monterey Park for input and to coordinate efforts. She also stressed the need to
  communicate concerns regarding an incoming development on Hellman Ave. in Monterey
  Park.

  Councilmember LEE supported exploration of a Preferred Parking District and discussed
  the concerns of residents. She also discussed the background of the hotel and concerns
  of residents. She urged greater communication regarding projects developed in
  neighboring cities.

  Councilmember MAZA supported Ms. Wang’s suggested direction to staff. He requested
  staff also research simple changes, such as extending red curbs.

  City Manager BINNQUIST provided clarification and stated that staff received an
  application for traffic calming measures and a traffic study would be conducted. She also
  urged the public to call the non-emergency Police department line regarding illegal parking
  issues.

  Action Taken:  City Council directed staff to conduct community outreach and
  survey to determine necessary boundaries of a Preferred Parking District adjacent to the
  Courtyard by Mariott and bring back the results to Council for discussion. No vote was
  required.

  48. APPROVAL OF A CHANGE ORDER TO CONTRACT FOR THE STORM DRAIN
  REHABILITATION PROJECT ON CARLOS AVENUE – F2M25-64, C2M26-5, M2M26-83

  On January 26, 2025, the City Council approved an award of Contract to Torres Sanitation
  Systems Construction for the Storm Drain Rehabilitation Project on Carlos Avenue in an
  8
6-22-26
   amount not to exceed $100,300.00 (C2M26-5). The Storm Drain Pipe Repair Project
  originally intended to rehabilitate a failing drainage line from 2027 Carlos Avenue to
  Montezuma Avenue. Due to the alignment passing multiple private properties, a
  trenchless pipe-lining method was selected to minimize surface disruption. However, pre-
  lining video inspections revealed severe structural deterioration undetected during initial
  assessments. Portions of the existing corrugated metal pipe were completely rusted out,
  leaving the pipe without a bottom section. This structural failure made immediate
  trenchless lining technically infeasible without structural stabilization. To resolve this issue
  and complete the project, the contractor would perform open-trench spot repairs at three
  distinct locations. This proposed Change Order would cover the direct costs of these
  structural spot repairs, alongside necessary site restoration efforts including concrete
  paving, soil leveling, and property cleaning.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved Change Order No. 1 for the Storm Drain
  Rehabilitation Project on Carlos Avenue, increasing Contract No. C2M26-5 with Torres
  Sanitation Systems Construction by $48,000.00 and bringing the total revised contract
  value to an amount not to exceed $148,300.00 to complete the project; appropriated
  $48,000.00 from the Safe Clean Water Program Fund to cover the change order; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M26-
  83)

 13.  APPROPRIATION FROM THE EQUIPMENT FUND RESERVE FOR THE PURCHASE
  OF ONE PATROL VEHICLE FOR THE ALHAMBRA POLICE DEPARTMENT – F2M25-
  17, M2M26-86

  On December 12, 2025, K-9 Patrol Vehicle Unit 560 was involved in a traffic collision while
  on duty, sustaining extensive damage. Following inspection, the insurance adjuster
  determined the vehicle to be a total loss. The California Joint Powers Insurance Authority
  (JPIA) issued an insurance settlement to the City in the amount of $50,892.95. Due to
  current market conditions and the cost of purchasing and outfitting a replacement patrol
  vehicle, the insurance proceeds were insufficient to cover the full replacement costs. Staff
  requested authorization for additional funds from the Equipment Fund Reserves to cover
  the shortfall of $10,669.14, which, after vehicle purchase and labor outfitting, was
  estimated at approximately $61,562.09.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved an appropriation of $10,669.14 from the
  Equipment Fund Reserve, for the purchase of one police patrol vehicle, and directed staff
  to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M26-86)

14.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR THE DESIGN OF
  A CHLORINATION SYSTEM AT MARENGO RESERVOIR – F2M26-31, RFP2M26-7

  The Marengo Reservoir Chlorination and Mixing Equipment System monitors the chlorine
  residual at each of the four reservoirs and maintains it at optimum levels. Due to the

  Community Development, each proposed amendment/addition was briefly described in a
